Affenpinscher.name: Affenpinscher
Affenpinscher.summary: A small, wiry-coated toy dog with a monkey-like face, originally bred to hunt rats in German kitchens and stables. It's confident and comical, with a big-dog attitude.
funFacts: "Affenpinscher" is German for "monkey terrier."
The French call it the "diablotin moustachu" — the mustached little devil.
An Affenpinscher named Banana Joe won Best in Show at Westminster in 2013.

Afghan Hound.name: Afghan Hound
Afghan Hound.summary: An ancient sighthound with a long, silky coat, bred to hunt in the mountains of Afghanistan. Aloof and dignified, it's also surprisingly silly with its family.
funFacts: Snuppy, the first cloned dog (South Korea, 2005), was an Afghan Hound.
Pablo Picasso had an Afghan Hound named Kabul who appears in some of his work.
The ring curl at the tip of its tail is a breed hallmark.

Airedale Terrier.name: Airedale Terrier
Airedale Terrier.summary: The largest of the terriers, the "King of Terriers" was bred in Yorkshire's Aire Valley to hunt otters and rats. It's clever, confident and tireless.
funFacts: Airedales carried messages and stood sentry for soldiers in World War I.
President Warren G. Harding's Airedale, Laddie Boy, reportedly had his own chair at Cabinet meetings.

Akita.name: Akita
Akita.summary: A large, powerful spitz breed from the mountains of northern Japan. Akitas are famously loyal and dignified, and reserved with strangers.
funFacts: Hachikō, the Akita who waited for his late owner at a Tokyo train station for nearly ten years, is Japan's symbol of loyalty.
Helen Keller brought the first Akita to the United States in 1937.

Alaskan Malamute.name: Alaskan Malamute
Alaskan Malamute.summary: One of the oldest Arctic sled dogs, bred by the Mahlemiut Inuit to haul heavy loads over long distances. Malamutes are strong, friendly and very vocal.
funFacts: It's the official state dog of Alaska.
Malamutes were built for strength and endurance, hauling freight rather than racing.
They're known for "talking" with woo-woo howls instead of barking.

American Bulldog.name: American Bulldog
American Bulldog.summary: A muscular, athletic bulldog descended from the working bulldogs of the American South, used on farms to catch livestock and guard property.
funFacts: The breed nearly vanished after World War II and was revived by breeders John D. Johnson and Alan Scott.
Chance, the wisecracking dog in Homeward Bound (1993), was an American Bulldog.

American Eskimo Dog.name: American Eskimo Dog
American Eskimo Dog.summary: A fluffy white spitz descended from German spitz dogs brought over by immigrants. Smart and eager to please, "Eskies" were stars of early 1900s circuses.
funFacts: It has nothing to do with the Inuit: it was renamed from "American Spitz" after World War I to avoid anti-German sentiment.
Traveling circuses featured Eskies doing tricks like walking a tightrope.

American Foxhound.name: American Foxhound
American Foxhound.summary: A lean, long-legged scent hound developed in colonial Virginia and Maryland for fox hunting. Easygoing at home, it's a tireless runner in the field.
funFacts: George Washington bred foxhounds and is often called a founder of the breed.
It's the state dog of Virginia.

American Hairless Terrier.name: American Hairless Terrier
American Hairless Terrier.summary: A small, active terrier descended from the Rat Terrier. Its hairless variety traces back to a single hairless puppy born in Louisiana in 1972.
funFacts: With no coat, it needs sunscreen in summer and a sweater in winter.
It's often suggested for people with dog allergies because it sheds so little.

American Pit Bull Terrier.name: American Pit Bull Terrier
American Pit Bull Terrier.summary: A muscular, athletic terrier descended from British bull-and-terrier dogs. Recognized by the UKC but not the AKC, it's known for its affection toward people.
funFacts: Pete the Pup, with the ring around his eye in the Our Gang (Little Rascals) comedies, was an American Pit Bull Terrier.
Pit bull–type dogs were popular American family dogs and mascots in the early 1900s.

American Staffordshire Terrier.name: American Staffordshire Terrier
American Staffordshire Terrier.summary: A stocky, muscular terrier recognized by the AKC in 1936, sharing its roots with the American Pit Bull Terrier. AmStaffs are confident and people-loving.
funFacts: "American" was added to its name in 1972 to tell it apart from the smaller Staffordshire Bull Terrier.
The AKC and UKC registered the same original dogs under different names.

American Water Spaniel.name: American Water Spaniel
American Water Spaniel.summary: A medium-sized brown spaniel with a curly coat, developed around the Great Lakes to retrieve waterfowl from small boats.
funFacts: It's the state dog of Wisconsin.
Its dense, curly coat sheds water, keeping it warm in cold lakes.

Anatolian Shepherd Dog.name: Anatolian Shepherd Dog
Anatolian Shepherd Dog.summary: A large, rugged livestock guardian from Turkey, bred for thousands of years to protect flocks from wolves. Calm and independent, it makes its own decisions.
funFacts: In Namibia, Anatolians guard livestock from cheetahs, which helps protect the cheetahs from farmers.
It's built to cover huge distances patrolling a flock's territory.

Appenzeller Sennenhund.name: Appenzeller Sennenhund
Appenzeller Sennenhund.summary: A medium-sized, tricolor Swiss mountain dog from the Appenzell region, bred to herd cattle and guard farms. It's lively, loud and loyal.
funFacts: It's one of four Swiss Sennenhund breeds, along with the Bernese, Entlebucher and Greater Swiss Mountain Dog.
Its tail curls tightly over its back, unlike the other Swiss mountain dogs.

Australian Cattle Dog.name: Australian Cattle Dog
Australian Cattle Dog.summary: A tough, compact herding dog developed in 19th-century Australia to move cattle over vast distances, partly from Dingo bloodlines.
funFacts: An Australian Cattle Dog named Bluey lived 29 years and 5 months, long the record for the oldest dog.
Puppies are born white; the blue or red speckled coat develops as they grow.
They're also called Blue Heelers or Red Heelers because they nip cattle's heels.

Australian Kelpie.name: Australian Kelpie
Australian Kelpie.summary: An energetic, intelligent herding dog developed in Australia to work sheep in harsh heat with little supervision.
funFacts: Kelpies are famous for running across the backs of packed sheep to reach the other side of the flock.
The breed is named after a 19th-century dog called Kelpie, itself named for a Scottish water spirit.

Australian Shepherd.name: Australian Shepherd
Australian Shepherd.summary: A medium-sized herding dog that, despite its name, was developed on ranches in the American West. Aussies are brilliant, energetic and need a job.
funFacts: Its ancestors likely came to America with Basque shepherds who had worked in Australia.
Many Aussies have two different-colored eyes.
The breed became popular through rodeos and horse shows in the 1950s.

Australian Terrier.name: Australian Terrier
Australian Terrier.summary: A small, sturdy terrier developed in Australia to control snakes and rodents and to keep watch over homes and farms.
funFacts: It was the first breed developed in Australia to be recognized and shown there.
The soft topknot of hair on its head is a breed signature.

Basenji.name: Basenji
Basenji.summary: An ancient hunting dog from Central Africa, known as the "barkless dog." Basenjis are curious, independent and remarkably cat-like.
funFacts: Instead of barking, Basenjis make a yodel-like sound called a "baroo."
They groom themselves like cats and have very little doggy odor.
Like wolves, females come into heat only once a year.

Basset Hound.name: Basset Hound
Basset Hound.summary: A short-legged French scent hound with long ears and a nose second only to the Bloodhound's. Patient and low-key at home, stubborn on a scent trail.
funFacts: "Basset" comes from the French "bas," meaning low.
Its long ears help sweep scents up toward its nose.
A Basset Hound is the mascot of Hush Puppies shoes.

Beagle.name: Beagle
Beagle.summary: A compact scent hound bred in England to hunt rabbits in packs. Merry and curious, it's one of America's most popular family dogs.
funFacts: Snoopy from Peanuts is a Beagle.
The USDA's "Beagle Brigade" sniffs out banned food and plants at U.S. airports.
A Beagle's nose has around 220 million scent receptors.

Bearded Collie.name: Bearded Collie
Bearded Collie.summary: A shaggy Scottish herding dog with a long coat and a "beard," known for its bouncy, exuberant personality.
funFacts: "Beardies" bounce while herding to see over the flock, and many still bounce when excited.
A Beardie's coat often lightens as a puppy and darkens again as it matures.

Beauceron.name: Beauceron
Beauceron.summary: A large black-and-tan French herding dog, the "Berger de Beauce," used for centuries to herd and guard sheep.
funFacts: Double dewclaws on the hind legs are a required breed trait.
Beaucerons served as messengers and sentries for the French army in both World Wars.

Bedlington Terrier.name: Bedlington Terrier
Bedlington Terrier.summary: A graceful terrier from northern England whose curly coat and arched back make it look like a little lamb.
funFacts: Despite its looks, it was bred by miners to hunt rats and badgers.
It's often described as "a lamb with the heart of a lion."

Belgian Malinois.name: Belgian Malinois
Belgian Malinois.summary: A short-coated Belgian shepherd that's intense, athletic and highly trainable, now a top choice for police and military work worldwide.
funFacts: A Malinois named Cairo took part in the 2011 raid on Osama bin Laden's compound.
It's named after the Belgian city of Malines (Mechelen).

Belgian Sheepdog.name: Belgian Sheepdog
Belgian Sheepdog.summary: The long-haired, all-black variety of Belgian shepherd, also called the Groenendael, bred to herd and guard sheep.
funFacts: It's named after the village of Groenendael near Brussels, where it was developed.
Belgian Sheepdogs served as messenger and ambulance dogs in World War I.

Belgian Tervuren.name: Belgian Tervuren
Belgian Tervuren.summary: The long-coated, fawn-to-mahogany variety of Belgian shepherd, elegant and energetic, named for the village of Tervuren.
funFacts: Its coat darkens with age, often with black tips called an "overlay."
Tervurens excel at agility, obedience and herding trials.

Bernedoodle.name: Bernedoodle
Bernedoodle.summary: A cross between a Bernese Mountain Dog and a Poodle, combining the Bernese's tricolor looks and gentle nature with the Poodle's lower-shedding coat.
funFacts: The first intentional Bernedoodles were bred in 2003 by Sherry Rupke in Ontario, Canada.
They come in tiny, miniature and standard sizes, depending on the Poodle parent.

Bernese Mountain Dog.name: Bernese Mountain Dog
Bernese Mountain Dog.summary: A large tricolor Swiss farm dog bred to pull carts, drive cattle and watch over farms in the canton of Bern. Gentle and good-natured.
funFacts: It's the only one of the four Swiss mountain dog breeds with a long coat.
Berners pulled carts of milk and cheese to market.

Bichon Frise.name: Bichon Frise
Bichon Frise.summary: A cheerful little white dog with a powder-puff coat, once a favorite of European royalty and later a street and circus performer.
funFacts: Its name is French for "curly lap dog."
Bichons traveled with sailors and were reportedly used as barter on trade voyages.
Their coat sheds very little.

Black Russian Terrier.name: Black Russian Terrier
Black Russian Terrier.summary: A large, powerful guard dog created by the Soviet Army's Red Star Kennel in the 1950s. Calm and confident, it's devoted to its family.
funFacts: It isn't a true terrier: about 17 breeds, including the Giant Schnauzer and Rottweiler, went into it.
It was bred to guard military installations.

Black and Tan Coonhound.name: Black and Tan Coonhound
Black and Tan Coonhound.summary: A big American scent hound bred to trail raccoons at night and "tree" them, baying until the hunter arrives.
funFacts: It was the first coonhound breed recognized by the AKC, in 1945.
Hunters can recognize their own coonhound's bay from far away.

Bloodhound.name: Bloodhound
Bloodhound.summary: The scent-tracking champion of the dog world, descended from hounds kept by monks at the Abbey of Saint-Hubert in Belgium.
funFacts: Bloodhound tracking evidence has been accepted in U.S. courts.
Its long ears and loose skin help trap scent around its face.
A Bloodhound named Tigger held the record for the longest dog ears, over 13 inches each.

Bluetick Coonhound.name: Bluetick Coonhound
Bluetick Coonhound.summary: A speckled-blue coonhound from the American South with a big voice and a cold-trailing nose.
funFacts: Its "blue ticked" look comes from black ticking over a white coat.
Smokey, the University of Tennessee's mascot, is a Bluetick Coonhound.

Border Collie.name: Border Collie
Border Collie.summary: Widely considered the most intelligent dog breed, bred on the border between Scotland and England to herd sheep with an intense stare.
funFacts: A Border Collie named Chaser learned the names of more than 1,000 toys.
They control sheep with an intense stare called "the eye."

Border Terrier.name: Border Terrier
Border Terrier.summary: A scrappy working terrier from the Cheviot Hills, small enough to follow foxes underground but leggy enough to keep up with horses.
funFacts: Its head is often described as "otter-like."
Border Terriers ran with foxhounds and bolted foxes from their dens.

Borzoi.name: Borzoi
Borzoi.summary: A tall, elegant Russian sighthound once kept by the aristocracy to hunt wolves. Calm and quiet indoors, lightning fast outside.
funFacts: "Borzoi" means "swift" in Russian.
The breed used to be called the Russian Wolfhound.

Boston Terrier.name: Boston Terrier
Boston Terrier.summary: A compact, tuxedo-coated companion developed in Boston in the late 1800s from bulldog and terrier crosses.
funFacts: Its black-and-white markings earned it the nickname "the American Gentleman."
It's the state dog of Massachusetts.
It was one of the first American breeds recognized by the AKC, in 1893.

Bouvier des Flandres.name: Bouvier des Flandres
Bouvier des Flandres.summary: A big, rough-coated Belgian farm dog bred to herd cattle, pull carts and guard the farm.
funFacts: Its name means "cow herder of Flanders."
President Ronald Reagan had a Bouvier named Lucky.

photo.author: Basco at Dutch Wikipedia (Original text: annekedirven@tiscali.nl)

Boxer.name: Boxer
Boxer.summary: A muscular, playful German breed descended from mastiff-type hunting dogs, known for its exuberance and patience with children.
funFacts: Boxers often stand on their hind legs and bat with their front paws when they play.
The Boxer was one of the first breeds used as a police dog in Germany.

Boykin Spaniel.name: Boykin Spaniel
Boykin Spaniel.summary: A small brown hunting spaniel developed in South Carolina to retrieve turkeys and ducks from small boats.
funFacts: It's the state dog of South Carolina.
The breed traces back to a stray spaniel named Dumpy, found near a church in Spartanburg in the early 1900s.

Briard.name: Briard
Briard.summary: An ancient French herding dog with a long, wavy coat, often described as "a heart wrapped in fur."
funFacts: Like the Beauceron, it has double dewclaws on its hind legs.
Briards served with the French army in World War I as sentries and in searching for the wounded.

photo.author: Birgit Balzer, Deutschland (uploaded by Caronna 17:00, 10 Feb 2005 (UTC))

Brittany.name: Brittany
Brittany.summary: An athletic, leggy bird dog from northwest France that both points and retrieves. Bright, upbeat and full of energy.
funFacts: Many Brittanys are born with a naturally short tail or none at all.
The AKC dropped "Spaniel" from its name in 1982 because it hunts more like a pointer.

Brussels Griffon.name: Brussels Griffon
Brussels Griffon.summary: A tiny Belgian toy dog with an almost human expression, originally kept by cab drivers to keep rats out of their stables.
funFacts: Verdell, the dog in As Good as It Gets (1997), was a Brussels Griffon.
Its expressive face is often said to have inspired the look of Star Wars' Ewoks.

Bull Terrier.name: Bull Terrier
Bull Terrier.summary: A muscular English terrier famous for its unique egg-shaped head and clownish, mischievous personality.
funFacts: Bullseye, Target's mascot, is a Bull Terrier.
General George S. Patton's Bull Terrier was named Willie.

Bullmastiff.name: Bullmastiff
Bullmastiff.summary: A powerful English guardian created in the 1800s by crossing Mastiffs and Bulldogs to stop poachers on large estates.
funFacts: Gamekeepers called it the "gamekeeper's night dog."
Bullmastiffs were trained to pin poachers down rather than bite them.

Cairn Terrier.name: Cairn Terrier
Cairn Terrier.summary: A shaggy little working terrier from the Scottish Highlands, bred to hunt foxes and rodents among piles of stones called cairns.
funFacts: Toto in The Wizard of Oz (1939) was played by a Cairn Terrier named Terry.
Cairns love to dig, a leftover from hunting among the rocks.

Canaan Dog.name: Canaan Dog
Canaan Dog.summary: An ancient pariah breed from the Middle East, re-established in the 1930s from semi-wild desert dogs to work as a guard and herding dog.
funFacts: It's the national dog of Israel.
Dogs of this type have survived on their own in the Negev desert for thousands of years.

photo.author: Canaan Dog, Hodowla Samorodok Hanaana http://www.ruscanaan.ru

Cane Corso.name: Cane Corso
Cane Corso.summary: A large Italian mastiff descended from Roman war dogs, used for centuries to guard property and hunt big game.
funFacts: Its name roughly means "bodyguard dog," from the Latin "cohors" (guardian).
The breed nearly vanished in the 20th century and was revived by Italian enthusiasts in the 1970s.

Cardigan Welsh Corgi.name: Cardigan Welsh Corgi
Cardigan Welsh Corgi.summary: The older of the two corgi breeds, a low-slung Welsh cattle dog distinguished by its long, foxy tail.
funFacts: Unlike the Pembroke, the Cardigan has a long tail and larger, rounder ears.
"Corgi" is usually translated from Welsh as "dwarf dog."

Cavalier King Charles Spaniel.name: Cavalier King Charles Spaniel
Cavalier King Charles Spaniel.summary: A gentle toy spaniel descended from the lapdogs of English royalty, especially King Charles II.
funFacts: King Charles II was said to take his spaniels almost everywhere, even to council meetings.
The red-and-white "Blenheim" color is named after Blenheim Palace.

Cavapoo.name: Cavapoo
Cavapoo.summary: A cross between a Cavalier King Charles Spaniel and a toy or miniature Poodle, bred as a gentle, lower-shedding companion.
funFacts: In Australia it's called the Cavoodle and is one of the country's most popular dogs.
Its coat can be wavy or tightly curled, depending on which parent it takes after.

Chesapeake Bay Retriever.name: Chesapeake Bay Retriever
Chesapeake Bay Retriever.summary: A powerful American retriever bred to haul ducks out of the icy waters of the Chesapeake Bay.
funFacts: The breed descends from two Newfoundland puppies rescued from a sinking ship off Maryland in 1807.
Its oily, wavy double coat is almost waterproof.
It's the state dog of Maryland.

Chihuahua.name: Chihuahua
Chihuahua.summary: The world's smallest dog breed, named after the Mexican state of Chihuahua and probably descended from the Techichi dogs of ancient Mexico.
funFacts: Chihuahuas have the largest brain relative to body size of any dog breed.
Many are born with a soft spot on the skull, called a molera, like a human baby.

photo.author: Bonnie van den Born, http://www.bonfoto.nl. The original uploader was Cwazi at Dutch Wikipedia.

Chinese Crested.name: Chinese Crested
Chinese Crested.summary: An elegant toy breed that comes in two varieties in the same litter: the mostly hairless Hairless and the fully coated Powderpuff.
Chinese Crested.origin: China (likely older African or Mexican roots)
funFacts: Hairless and Powderpuff puppies can be born in the same litter.
Chinese Cresteds have won the World's Ugliest Dog Contest several times.

Chow Chow.name: Chow Chow
Chow Chow.summary: An ancient Chinese breed with a lion-like mane and an aloof, almost cat-like personality.
funFacts: Chow Chows have blue-black tongues.
Sigmund Freud's Chow, Jofi, often sat in on his therapy sessions.

Clumber Spaniel.name: Clumber Spaniel
Clumber Spaniel.summary: The heaviest of the spaniels, a long, low, mostly white gundog developed at Clumber Park, the Duke of Newcastle's estate.
funFacts: It's named after Clumber Park in Nottinghamshire.
King Edward VII kept Clumbers at the royal Sandringham estate.

Cockapoo.name: Cockapoo
Cockapoo.summary: A cross between a Cocker Spaniel and a Poodle, one of the oldest "designer" dogs, dating back to the 1950s in the United States.
funFacts: It's considered one of the first popular designer crossbreeds.
In the UK, Cockapoos regularly rank among the most popular dogs.

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. BetacommandBot assumed (based on copyright claims).

Cocker Spaniel.name: Cocker Spaniel
Cocker Spaniel.summary: The smallest of the AKC's sporting dogs, a merry American spaniel with a long, silky coat, developed from the English Cocker.
funFacts: Lady in Disney's Lady and the Tramp is an American Cocker Spaniel.
"Cocker" comes from their use in hunting woodcock.

Collie.name: Collie
Collie.summary: A graceful Scottish herding dog with a flowing coat, made world-famous by the Lassie films and TV series.
funFacts: Lassie was played by male Collies, starting with a dog named Pal.
Queen Victoria helped make Collies fashionable in the 1860s.

Curly-Coated Retriever.name: Curly-Coated Retriever
Curly-Coated Retriever.summary: One of the oldest retriever breeds, covered in tight, crisp curls that shed water and brambles.
funFacts: It's the tallest of the retriever breeds.
Its tight curls protect it in icy water and thick cover.

Dachshund.name: Dachshund
Dachshund.summary: A long-bodied, short-legged German hound bred to dig into badger dens, now one of the world's most popular companions.
funFacts: "Dachshund" means "badger dog" in German.
A Dachshund named Waldi was the first official Olympic mascot (Munich, 1972).
They come in three coat types: smooth, wirehaired and longhaired.

Dalmatian.name: Dalmatian
Dalmatian.summary: A spotted coach dog named after Dalmatia in Croatia, famous for running alongside horse-drawn carriages and fire engines.
funFacts: Dalmatian puppies are born pure white; their spots appear as they grow.
They became firehouse mascots because they guarded and calmed the horses that pulled fire wagons.

Dandie Dinmont Terrier.name: Dandie Dinmont Terrier
Dandie Dinmont Terrier.summary: A long, low terrier from the Scottish Borders with a big, fluffy topknot, bred to hunt otters and badgers.
funFacts: It's the only breed named after a fictional character: Dandie Dinmont in Sir Walter Scott's 1815 novel Guy Mannering.
It's one of the rarest terrier breeds today.

Dingo.name: Dingo
Dingo.summary: Australia's wild dog, descended from domestic dogs that arrived with people thousands of years ago and returned to the wild.
funFacts: The Dingo Fence, built to keep dingoes away from sheep, stretches about 5,600 km across Australia.
Dingoes have unusually flexible joints and can rotate their wrists and climb.

Doberman Pinscher.name: Doberman Pinscher
Doberman Pinscher.summary: A sleek, powerful guard dog developed in Germany in the 1890s. Dobermans are loyal, alert and highly trainable.
funFacts: Tax collector Louis Dobermann bred the first Dobermans to protect him on his rounds.
A Doberman named Kurt is honored at the U.S. War Dog Cemetery on Guam after dying in the 1944 battle there.

Dogue de Bordeaux.name: Dogue de Bordeaux
Dogue de Bordeaux.summary: A massive French mastiff with a huge head and a red coat, used historically to guard estates and drive cattle.
funFacts: Hooch, Tom Hanks's co-star in Turner & Hooch (1989), was a Dogue de Bordeaux.
It has one of the largest heads relative to its body of any breed.

English Bulldog.name: English Bulldog
English Bulldog.summary: A stocky, wrinkled English breed with a pushed-in face, once used in bull-baiting and later reshaped into a gentle, calm companion.
funFacts: The Bulldog is the mascot of the U.S. Marine Corps and many universities, including Yale.
Because of their large heads, most Bulldog puppies are born by C-section.

English Cocker Spaniel.name: English Cocker Spaniel
English Cocker Spaniel.summary: A compact British gundog bred to flush and retrieve woodcock, a little taller and leaner than its American cousin.
funFacts: The AKC split the English and American Cocker into separate breeds in 1946.
Its constantly wagging tail earned it the nickname "merry cocker."

English Foxhound.name: English Foxhound
English Foxhound.summary: A sturdy pack hound bred for centuries by English hunts, with breeding records going back to the 1700s.
funFacts: Some English Foxhound packs have stud books dating back to the 1700s.
It's one of the least common breeds registered with the AKC.

English Setter.name: English Setter
English Setter.summary: A gentle, elegant bird dog with a speckled coat, bred to "set" (crouch) when it finds game birds.
funFacts: Its speckled coat pattern is called "belton," after a village in Northumberland.
Setters got their name from crouching low to show hunters where birds were hiding.

English Springer Spaniel.name: English Springer Spaniel
English Springer Spaniel.summary: A medium-sized British gundog bred to "spring" (flush) game birds into the air for hunters.
funFacts: Millie, George H. W. Bush's Springer, "wrote" a bestselling book about life in the White House.
Springers are widely used as detection dogs by police and customs agencies.

English Toy Spaniel.name: English Toy Spaniel
English Toy Spaniel.summary: A small, flat-faced spaniel, called the King Charles Spaniel in the UK, that has been a royal lapdog since the Tudor era.
funFacts: In the 1920s, breeders recreated the longer-nosed spaniels in old paintings, giving rise to the Cavalier King Charles Spaniel.
Legend says Mary, Queen of Scots had her toy spaniel with her at her execution.

Entlebucher Mountain Dog.name: Entlebucher Mountain Dog
Entlebucher Mountain Dog.summary: The smallest of the four Swiss mountain dogs, a nimble tricolor cattle herder from the Entlebuch valley.
funFacts: It's the smallest of the four Swiss Sennenhund breeds.
The AKC recognized it only in 2011.

Field Spaniel.name: Field Spaniel
Field Spaniel.summary: A rare, medium-sized British spaniel with a glossy coat, bred to hunt birds in dense cover.
funFacts: The breed nearly disappeared in the early 1900s after being bred for exaggerated length.
It's one of the rarest sporting breeds registered with the AKC.

Fila Brasileiro.name: Fila Brasileiro
Fila Brasileiro.summary: A huge Brazilian mastiff known for its tracking ability and fierce devotion to its family.
funFacts: It moves both legs on one side at the same time, a "camel pace" that's unusual in dogs.
It's banned or restricted in several countries, including the UK.

Finnish Spitz.name: Finnish Spitz
Finnish Spitz.summary: Finland's national dog, a fox-red spitz that hunts birds by barking to mark the tree where they perch.
funFacts: Finland holds barking contests for the breed; top barkers can bark more than 100 times a minute.
It's the national dog of Finland.

Flat-Coated Retriever.name: Flat-Coated Retriever
Flat-Coated Retriever.summary: A sleek black or liver retriever known for its lifelong, puppy-like enthusiasm.
funFacts: Owners call it the "Peter Pan" of retrievers because it never seems to grow up.
It was England's most popular retriever before the Labrador and Golden took over.

French Bulldog.name: French Bulldog
French Bulldog.summary: A compact companion with signature "bat ears," developed in France from toy bulldogs brought over by English lace workers.
funFacts: In 2022 it became America's most popular breed, ending the Labrador's 31-year run.
Most Frenchies can't swim well because of their heavy front ends.

German Pinscher.name: German Pinscher
German Pinscher.summary: A sleek, medium-sized German ratter and watchdog, and an ancestor of the Doberman and the Miniature Pinscher.
funFacts: It helped create both the Doberman Pinscher and the Miniature Pinscher.
The breed nearly disappeared after the two World Wars.

German Shepherd.name: German Shepherd
German Shepherd.summary: A versatile, intelligent German herding dog that has become the world's leading police, military and service dog.
funFacts: The breed was founded by Captain Max von Stephanitz in 1899.
Rin Tin Tin, rescued from a World War I battlefield, became a Hollywood star.
The first U.S. guide dog for the blind, Buddy, was a German Shepherd.

German Shorthaired Pointer.name: German Shorthaired Pointer
German Shorthaired Pointer.summary: An all-purpose German hunting dog that points, retrieves and tracks on land and in water.
funFacts: A GSP named CJ won Best in Show at Westminster in 2016.
Their webbed feet make them strong swimmers.

German Wirehaired Pointer.name: German Wirehaired Pointer
German Wirehaired Pointer.summary: A rugged, all-weather German gundog with a wiry, water-resistant coat and a distinctive beard.
funFacts: In Germany it's called the Deutsch Drahthaar and is one of the most popular hunting dogs.
Its harsh coat protects it from brambles and icy water.

Giant Schnauzer.name: Giant Schnauzer
Giant Schnauzer.summary: The largest of the three schnauzers, developed in Bavaria to drive cattle and later used as a police and guard dog.
funFacts: It was once known as the Munich Schnauzer.
"Schnauzer" comes from the German word for snout.

Glen of Imaal Terrier.name: Glen of Imaal Terrier
Glen of Imaal Terrier.summary: A short-legged, sturdy Irish terrier from the remote Glen of Imaal in County Wicklow.
funFacts: Glens were reportedly used as "turnspit dogs," running in wheels to turn meat roasting over a fire.
It's one of the rarest terrier breeds in the world.

Golden Retriever.name: Golden Retriever
Golden Retriever.summary: A friendly, eager-to-please Scottish gundog bred to retrieve waterfowl, now one of the world's most popular family dogs.
funFacts: The breed was developed by Lord Tweedmouth in the Scottish Highlands in the mid-1800s.
Goldens have such a "soft mouth" that many can carry a raw egg without breaking it.

photo.author: Dukedestiny01.jpg: "Janneke Vreugdenhil" derivative work: Anka Friedrich ([[User talk:Ankaaswe Trix Friedrich|talk]])

Goldendoodle.name: Goldendoodle
Goldendoodle.summary: A cross between a Golden Retriever and a Poodle, popular since the 1990s as a friendly, lower-shedding family dog.
funFacts: Breeders use labels like F1 (Golden × Poodle) and F1B (F1 × Poodle) to describe the mix.
Goldendoodles come in toy, miniature, medium and standard sizes.

Gordon Setter.name: Gordon Setter
Gordon Setter.summary: The heaviest of the setters, a black-and-tan Scottish bird dog made famous by the 4th Duke of Gordon.
funFacts: The breed was developed at Gordon Castle in the 1820s.
It's the only black-and-tan setter breed.

Great Dane.name: Great Dane
Great Dane.summary: A giant German breed once used to hunt wild boar, now known as the "Apollo of dogs" for its gentle, patient nature.
funFacts: A Great Dane named Zeus was the tallest dog on record, 44 inches at the shoulder.
Scooby-Doo and Marmaduke are both Great Danes.

Great Pyrenees.name: Great Pyrenees
Great Pyrenees.summary: A large, white livestock guardian from the Pyrenees mountains, bred to protect sheep from wolves and bears.
funFacts: King Louis XIV reportedly named it the Royal Dog of France in 1675.
Like the Beauceron and Briard, it has double dewclaws on its hind legs.

Greater Swiss Mountain Dog.name: Greater Swiss Mountain Dog
Greater Swiss Mountain Dog.summary: The largest and oldest of the Swiss mountain dogs, a strong tricolor drafter once called "the poor man's horse."
funFacts: It pulled heavy carts of meat and dairy for farmers and butchers.
It's the largest of the four Swiss Sennenhund breeds.

Greyhound.name: Greyhound
Greyhound.summary: The fastest dog breed, a sleek sighthound with ancient roots, often adopted today as a gentle retired racer.
funFacts: Greyhounds can reach about 45 mph.
Despite their speed, they're famous for lounging indoors — fans call them "45-mph couch potatoes."

Havanese.name: Havanese
Havanese.summary: Cuba's national dog, a cheerful little companion with a silky coat, descended from the Bichon family.
funFacts: It's the national dog of Cuba.
Most modern Havanese descend from about 11 dogs brought out of Cuba after the revolution.

Ibizan Hound.name: Ibizan Hound
Ibizan Hound.summary: A lean, deer-like hound from the Spanish island of Ibiza, bred to hunt rabbits using sight, scent and hearing.
funFacts: Ibizan Hounds can leap remarkably high from a standstill.
Their large, upright ears help them pinpoint prey hiding in brush.

Icelandic Sheepdog.name: Icelandic Sheepdog
Icelandic Sheepdog.summary: Iceland's only native dog, a cheerful spitz brought over by the Vikings more than 1,000 years ago.
funFacts: It arrived in Iceland with Viking settlers between 874 and 930 AD.
Many have double dewclaws on their hind legs.

Irish Red and White Setter.name: Irish Red and White Setter
Irish Red and White Setter.summary: The older of Ireland's two setters, a red-and-white bird dog that was nearly lost as the solid-red Irish Setter grew popular.
funFacts: It predates the all-red Irish Setter.
The breed was close to extinction by the early 1900s and was revived in the 1920s.

Irish Setter.name: Irish Setter
Irish Setter.summary: A glamorous mahogany-red bird dog from Ireland, known for its boundless energy and friendly nature.
funFacts: Disney's Big Red (1962) starred an Irish Setter.
Richard Nixon's Irish Setter, King Timahoe, lived in the White House.

photo.author: Luis Miguel Bugallo Sánchez (Lmbuga Commons)(Lmbuga Galipedia) Publicada por/Publish by: Luis Miguel Bugallo Sánchez

Irish Terrier.name: Irish Terrier
Irish Terrier.summary: A fiery, red-coated Irish terrier nicknamed the "Daredevil," used as a farm dog, guard and ratter.
funFacts: Irish Terriers carried messages for soldiers in World War I.
It's one of the oldest terrier breeds.

Irish Water Spaniel.name: Irish Water Spaniel
Irish Water Spaniel.summary: The tallest spaniel, a curly, liver-coated Irish water retriever with a distinctive smooth tail.
funFacts: Its thin, smooth tail earned it the nickname "rat tail."
It's often called the clown of the spaniel family.

Irish Wolfhound.name: Irish Wolfhound
Irish Wolfhound.summary: The tallest of all dog breeds, an ancient Irish sighthound once used to hunt wolves and in war, now a gentle giant.
funFacts: It's the tallest AKC breed; males stand at least 32 inches at the shoulder.
Despite their history as war dogs, Wolfhounds are famously gentle and easygoing.

Italian Greyhound.name: Italian Greyhound
Italian Greyhound.summary: A miniature sighthound beloved by Renaissance nobility, with all of a Greyhound's grace in a much smaller package.
funFacts: Frederick the Great of Prussia loved his Italian Greyhounds and was buried near them.
Small greyhounds like these appear in art from ancient Rome and Pompeii.

Jack Russell Terrier.name: Jack Russell Terrier
Jack Russell Terrier.summary: A small, tireless fox-hunting terrier developed by the Reverend John "Jack" Russell in 19th-century England.
funFacts: Eddie on the TV show Frasier was played by a Jack Russell named Moose.
The AKC recognizes two related breeds: the Parson Russell Terrier and the Russell Terrier.

Japanese Chin.name: Japanese Chin
Japanese Chin.summary: An aristocratic toy breed long cherished by Japanese nobility, known for its cat-like grace and charm.
funFacts: Many Chins do the "Chin spin," twirling in circles when excited.
Commodore Perry is said to have brought Chins back from Japan in the 1850s, some as gifts for Queen Victoria.

Japanese Spitz.name: Japanese Spitz
Japanese Spitz.summary: A small, fluffy white spitz developed in Japan in the 1920s and 1930s from German Spitz ancestors.
funFacts: It looks like a miniature Samoyed but is a separate breed.
Its stand-off white coat is surprisingly good at shedding dirt.

Keeshond.name: Keeshond
Keeshond.summary: A fluffy Dutch spitz with distinctive "spectacles" around its eyes, once the watchdog of barges on Dutch canals.
funFacts: It was the symbol of the Dutch Patriot party in the 1780s, named after its leader Kees de Gyselaer.
The dark lines from its eyes to its ears look like spectacles.

Kerry Blue Terrier.name: Kerry Blue Terrier
Kerry Blue Terrier.summary: An Irish all-purpose farm terrier whose soft, wavy coat turns blue-gray as it matures.
funFacts: Puppies are born black; the coat clears to blue between about 6 and 24 months.
It's often called the national terrier of Ireland.

Komondor.name: Komondor
Komondor.summary: A large Hungarian livestock guardian covered in white, corded "dreadlocks" that let it blend in with the flock.
funFacts: A mature Komondor's cords can reach the ground and weigh around 15 pounds.
The coat camouflages it among sheep and protects it from wolf bites.

Kuvasz.name: Kuvasz
Kuvasz.summary: A large, white Hungarian guardian dog once kept by royalty to protect estates and livestock.
funFacts: King Matthias I of Hungary reportedly trusted his Kuvaszok more than his human bodyguards.
Its white coat helped shepherds tell it apart from wolves at night.

Labradoodle.name: Labradoodle
Labradoodle.summary: A cross between a Labrador Retriever and a Poodle, first bred in Australia in 1989 as a low-shedding guide dog.
funFacts: Wally Conron bred the first Labradoodle at Royal Guide Dogs Victoria for a blind woman whose husband was allergic to dogs.
Conron later said he regretted starting the "designer dog" craze.

Labrador Retriever.name: Labrador Retriever
Labrador Retriever.summary: A friendly, outgoing retriever from Newfoundland, refined in Britain, and for decades America's most popular dog breed.
funFacts: Labs were America's most popular breed for 31 years in a row (1991–2021).
Webbed toes and a thick "otter tail" that works like a rudder make them great swimmers.

Lakeland Terrier.name: Lakeland Terrier
Lakeland Terrier.summary: A compact, wire-coated terrier from England's Lake District, bred to protect sheep from foxes.
funFacts: A Lakeland named Stingray won Best in Show at both Crufts (1967) and Westminster (1968).
It was bred to work in the rocky fells where foxes raided sheep.

Leonberger.name: Leonberger
Leonberger.summary: A giant, gentle German companion bred in the town of Leonberg, with a lion-like mane and a love of water.
funFacts: Breeder Heinrich Essig is said to have created it to resemble the lion on Leonberg's coat of arms.
Leonbergers have webbed feet and are used in water rescue.

Lhasa Apso.name: Lhasa Apso
Lhasa Apso.summary: An ancient Tibetan breed that guarded Buddhist monasteries from the inside, alerting monks to intruders.
funFacts: Tibetans called it "Abso Seng Kye" — the bark lion sentinel dog.
The Dalai Lama traditionally gave Lhasa Apsos as gifts to visiting dignitaries.

Lowchen.name: Lowchen
Lowchen.summary: A small, lively companion whose traditional "lion trim" earned it the nickname "little lion dog."
funFacts: "Löwchen" is German for "little lion."
In 1973 it was listed as one of the rarest dog breeds in the world.

Maltese.name: Maltese
Maltese.summary: An ancient toy breed with a floor-length white coat, pampered as a lapdog since the days of ancient Greece and Rome.
funFacts: The Maltese has been a pampered pet for more than 2,000 years.
It has no undercoat, so it sheds very little.

Maltipoo.name: Maltipoo
Maltipoo.summary: A cross between a Maltese and a toy or miniature Poodle, bred as a small, lower-shedding companion.
funFacts: Many Maltipoos keep a puppy-like look their whole lives.
Their small size makes them a popular choice for apartment living.

Manchester Terrier.name: Manchester Terrier
Manchester Terrier.summary: A sleek black-and-tan terrier developed in Manchester, England, to kill rats and chase rabbits.
funFacts: It comes in two varieties: Standard and Toy.
The tan markings on its front legs include black "thumbprints."

Mastiff.name: Mastiff
Mastiff.summary: A massive, ancient English guardian, one of the heaviest dog breeds in the world, with a calm, dignified nature.
funFacts: An English Mastiff named Zorba weighed 343 pounds in 1989, a record for the heaviest dog.
Mastiffs are said to have come to America on the Mayflower.

Miniature Pinscher.name: Miniature Pinscher
Miniature Pinscher.summary: A small, sleek German toy dog nicknamed the "King of Toys" for its confident, high-stepping strut.
funFacts: It isn't a mini Doberman: the Min Pin is the older breed.
Its high-stepping walk is called a "hackney gait," like a carriage horse's.

Miniature Schnauzer.name: Miniature Schnauzer
Miniature Schnauzer.summary: The smallest schnauzer, a bearded German farm dog bred to catch rats, now a popular family companion.
funFacts: It was developed by crossing Standard Schnauzers with smaller breeds like the Affenpinscher.
Its bushy beard and eyebrows give it a wise old-man look.

Neapolitan Mastiff.name: Neapolitan Mastiff
Neapolitan Mastiff.summary: A massive Italian guardian with heavy wrinkles and loose skin, descended from the war dogs of ancient Rome.
funFacts: Fang, Hagrid's dog in the Harry Potter films, was played by Neapolitan Mastiffs.
Its loose skin and folds were thought to protect it from bites.

Newfoundland.name: Newfoundland
Newfoundland.summary: A giant, sweet-natured Canadian working dog bred to help fishermen haul nets and rescue people from the sea.
funFacts: A Newfoundland named Seaman traveled with the Lewis and Clark expedition.
Nana, the nursemaid dog in Peter Pan, is a Newfoundland.
Webbed feet and a water-resistant coat make them powerful swimmers.

Norfolk Terrier.name: Norfolk Terrier
Norfolk Terrier.summary: One of the smallest working terriers, a sturdy little ratter from East Anglia with folded ears.
funFacts: It's nearly identical to the Norwich Terrier, except its ears fold down.
Norfolks and Norwiches were shown as one breed until 1964 in the UK.

photo.author: Nutak at Dutch Wikipedia (Original text: NTCN, mw.G. Hajnova)

Norwegian Buhund.name: Norwegian Buhund
Norwegian Buhund.summary: A Nordic spitz-type farm dog used for centuries to herd sheep and guard homesteads.
funFacts: Remains of Buhund-type dogs have been found in Viking graves.
"Bu" refers to the farm or homestead in Norwegian.

Norwegian Elkhound.name: Norwegian Elkhound
Norwegian Elkhound.summary: An ancient Norwegian hunting spitz bred to track moose and hold them at bay with loud barking.
funFacts: "Elkhound" comes from the Norwegian "elghund" — moose dog.
It's often called Norway's national dog.

Norwegian Lundehund.name: Norwegian Lundehund
Norwegian Lundehund.summary: A rare, flexible Norwegian spitz bred to climb sea cliffs and pull puffins from their nests.
funFacts: It has six toes on each foot.
It can tip its head backward to touch its spine and spread its front legs straight out to the sides.

Norwich Terrier.name: Norwich Terrier
Norwich Terrier.summary: A tiny, prick-eared English terrier bred to hunt rats and foxes, known for its fearless, cheerful attitude.
funFacts: It's the prick-eared twin of the Norfolk Terrier.
A Norwich won Best in Show at Westminster in 1998.

Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever.name: Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever
Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever.summary: The smallest retriever, a red Canadian dog that lures ducks within range by playing at the water's edge.
funFacts: "Tolling" means luring: the dog's playful splashing draws curious ducks closer.
It's the provincial dog of Nova Scotia.

Old English Sheepdog.name: Old English Sheepdog
Old English Sheepdog.summary: A big, shaggy English drover's dog famous for its profuse coat and rolling, bear-like gait.
funFacts: Drovers' dogs traditionally had docked tails, which earned the breed the nickname "bobtail."
Paul McCartney's Old English Sheepdog, Martha, inspired the Beatles song "Martha My Dear."

Otterhound.name: Otterhound
Otterhound.summary: A large, shaggy British scent hound bred to hunt otters, now one of the world's rarest breeds.
funFacts: There are thought to be fewer than 1,000 Otterhounds in the world.
Otter hunting was banned in England in 1978, leaving the breed without its job.

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Machinecha~commonswiki assumed (based on copyright claims).

Papillon.name: Papillon
Papillon.summary: A dainty toy spaniel named for its butterfly-wing ears, a favorite of European royalty for centuries.
funFacts: "Papillon" is French for butterfly.
Papillons appear in many Renaissance paintings, often on the laps of noblewomen.

Pekingese.name: Pekingese
Pekingese.summary: A lion-like toy breed that was once reserved for the Chinese imperial court.
funFacts: A Pekingese named Sun Yat-sen was one of three dogs to survive the sinking of the Titanic.
Legend says stealing one from the imperial palace was punishable by death.

Pembroke Welsh Corgi.name: Pembroke Welsh Corgi
Pembroke Welsh Corgi.summary: A short-legged Welsh cattle herder with a foxy face, famous as Queen Elizabeth II's favorite breed.
funFacts: Queen Elizabeth II owned more than 30 Pembroke Corgis during her reign.
Welsh legend says fairies rode corgis, leaving a "saddle" mark on their coats.

Petit Basset Griffon Vendeen.name: Petit Basset Griffon Vendeen
Petit Basset Griffon Vendeen.summary: A small, rough-coated French scent hound bred to hunt rabbits in the rugged Vendée region.
funFacts: Its name describes it: small (petit), low (basset), rough-coated (griffon), from the Vendée.
A PBGV named Buddy Holly won Best in Show at Westminster in 2023.

Pharaoh Hound.name: Pharaoh Hound
Pharaoh Hound.summary: An elegant rabbit-hunting hound from Malta, known for its amber eyes and glowing red coat.
funFacts: When excited, its nose and ears flush pink — it "blushes."
It's the national dog of Malta, where it's called Kelb tal-Fenek, "rabbit dog."

Plott Hound.name: Plott Hound
Plott Hound.summary: A brindle American hound descended from German boar-hunting dogs brought over by the Plott family in 1750.
funFacts: It's the state dog of North Carolina.
Unlike most American hounds, it descends from German rather than British dogs.

Pointer.name: Pointer
Pointer.summary: The classic English bird dog that freezes in a "point" to show hunters where game is hiding.
funFacts: Many Pointer puppies point instinctively at a few weeks old, with no training.
The dog in the Westminster Kennel Club's logo is a Pointer named Sensation.

Pomeranian.name: Pomeranian
Pomeranian.summary: A tiny, fluffy spitz bred down from larger sled-type dogs and made popular by Queen Victoria.
funFacts: Queen Victoria's love of small Pomeranians helped shrink the breed to its modern size.
Two Pomeranians survived the sinking of the Titanic.

Pomsky.name: Pomsky
Pomsky.summary: A cross between a Pomeranian and a Siberian Husky, bred to look like a miniature husky.
funFacts: Pomskies are usually bred by artificial insemination, with the Husky as the mother.
The mix shot to fame through viral photos online in the early 2010s.

Poodle.name: Poodle
Poodle.summary: A highly intelligent breed in three sizes, originally a German water retriever and now the national dog of France.
funFacts: The fancy show clip started as a practical cut to lighten the coat for swimming while keeping joints warm.
"Poodle" comes from the German "Pudel," related to splashing in water.
Poodles are widely ranked as the second most intelligent breed, after the Border Collie.

photo.author: Tim Wilson from Blaine, MN, USA

Portuguese Water Dog.name: Portuguese Water Dog
Portuguese Water Dog.summary: A curly-coated Portuguese fisherman's dog that herded fish into nets and carried messages between boats.
funFacts: Bo and Sunny, the Obama family's dogs, were Portuguese Water Dogs.
Webbed feet and a waterproof coat make them excellent swimmers.

Pug.name: Pug
Pug.summary: An ancient Chinese toy breed with a wrinkled face and curled tail, loved for its comedic personality.
funFacts: A Pug named Pompey is said to have saved William of Orange from assassins in 1572.
The breed's motto is "Multum in parvo" — a lot in a little.

photo.author: Mops_oct09.jpg: Dagur Brynjólfsson from Hafnarfjordur, Iceland; derivative work: Anka Friedrich

Redbone Coonhound.name: Redbone Coonhound
Redbone Coonhound.summary: A sleek, solid-red American coonhound, a fast hunter in rough terrain and an easygoing family dog.
funFacts: Old Dan and Little Ann in Where the Red Fern Grows were Redbone Coonhounds.
Redbones are nimble enough to hunt in swamps and mountains alike.

Rhodesian Ridgeback.name: Rhodesian Ridgeback
Rhodesian Ridgeback.summary: A muscular African hound developed in Rhodesia (now Zimbabwe) to track lions and hold them at bay.
funFacts: The ridge along its back is hair growing in the opposite direction from the rest of the coat.
It was nicknamed the "African Lion Hound."

Rottweiler.name: Rottweiler
Rottweiler.summary: A powerful German breed descended from Roman drover dogs, used to herd cattle and pull butchers' carts in the town of Rottweil.
funFacts: Butchers in Rottweil are said to have tied money pouches to their dogs' collars to keep the money safe.
Rottweilers were among the first police dogs.

photo.author: Dr. Manfred Herrmann Allgemeiner Deutscher Rottweiler-Klub (ADRK) e.V. http://www.ADRK.de

Saint Bernard.name: Saint Bernard
Saint Bernard.summary: A giant Alpine rescue dog bred by monks at the Great St Bernard Hospice to find travelers lost in the snow.
funFacts: A St. Bernard named Barry is credited with saving more than 40 people in the early 1800s.
The famous brandy barrel around the neck is mostly a myth, popularized by a painting.
Beethoven, star of the 1992 family movie, is a St. Bernard.

Saluki.name: Saluki
Saluki.summary: One of the oldest dog breeds, a graceful desert sighthound bred to hunt gazelles across the Middle East.
funFacts: Saluki-like dogs appear in ancient Egyptian tomb paintings.
Bedouin tribes prized Salukis so highly they called them el hor, "the noble one."

Samoyed.name: Samoyed
Samoyed.summary: A fluffy white Siberian spitz bred by the Samoyedic peoples to herd reindeer, pull sleds and keep them warm at night.
funFacts: The upturned corners of its mouth, the "Sammy smile," are said to keep drool from freezing into icicles.
Samoyeds pulled sleds on early polar expeditions, including Roald Amundsen's.

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Pleple2000 assumed (based on copyright claims).

Schipperke.name: Schipperke
Schipperke.summary: A small black Belgian dog that guarded canal barges and caught rats, nicknamed the "little captain."
funFacts: Its name is Flemish for "little boatman" or "little captain."
Its ruff and tailless rear give it a distinctive fox-like silhouette.

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. 鏑木對馬守 assumed (based on copyright claims).

Scottish Deerhound.name: Scottish Deerhound
Scottish Deerhound.summary: A tall, rough-coated Scottish sighthound bred to hunt red deer, once owned only by nobility.
funFacts: In the Middle Ages, no one below the rank of earl was allowed to own one.
A Deerhound named Hickory won Best in Show at Westminster in 2011.

Scottish Terrier.name: Scottish Terrier
Scottish Terrier.summary: A sturdy, bearded Highland terrier bred to hunt foxes and badgers, nicknamed the "Diehard."
funFacts: Franklin D. Roosevelt's Scottie, Fala, is part of his memorial in Washington, D.C.
The Scottie is one of the playing pieces in Monopoly.

Sealyham Terrier.name: Sealyham Terrier
Sealyham Terrier.summary: A sturdy white Welsh terrier bred to hunt otters, badgers and foxes, now a rare breed.
funFacts: Alfred Hitchcock walks his own two Sealyhams in his cameo in The Birds (1963).
It was developed by Captain John Edwardes on his Sealyham estate in the 1800s.

Shar-Pei.name: Shar-Pei
Shar-Pei.summary: An ancient Chinese guard dog famous for its deep wrinkles, hippo-shaped muzzle and blue-black tongue.
funFacts: In 1978 Guinness listed it as the world's rarest dog breed.
"Shar-Pei" means "sand skin," for its rough, bristly coat.

Shetland Sheepdog.name: Shetland Sheepdog
Shetland Sheepdog.summary: A small, agile herding dog from Scotland's Shetland Islands that looks like a miniature Rough Collie.
funFacts: Shelties were bred to keep sheep, ponies and birds out of crofters' gardens.
They're consistently among the top breeds in obedience and agility competitions.

Shiba Inu.name: Shiba Inu
Shiba Inu.summary: Japan's oldest and smallest native spitz, a bold, fox-like hunting dog with a famously independent streak.
funFacts: The "Doge" meme and the Dogecoin cryptocurrency feature a Shiba Inu named Kabosu.
Shibas are known for the "Shiba scream," a dramatic high-pitched protest.

Shih Tzu.name: Shih Tzu
Shih Tzu.summary: A "little lion dog" bred as a palace companion for Chinese royalty, with a flowing coat and a sweet nature.
funFacts: "Shih Tzu" means "little lion" in Mandarin.
Nearly all modern Shih Tzus descend from 14 dogs used to rebuild the breed in the 20th century.

Siberian Husky.name: Siberian Husky
Siberian Husky.summary: A medium-sized sled dog bred by the Chukchi people of Siberia for endurance in extreme cold.
funFacts: Huskies including Balto and Togo relayed diphtheria medicine to Nome, Alaska, in the 1925 "Great Race of Mercy."
Many Huskies have blue eyes, or one blue and one brown.

Silky Terrier.name: Silky Terrier
Silky Terrier.summary: A small Australian terrier with a glossy blue-and-tan coat, bred from Yorkshire and Australian Terriers.
funFacts: It's often mistaken for a Yorkie but is a bit larger, with a more wedge-shaped head.
Despite its Toy-group size, it was bred to hunt snakes and rodents.

Smooth Fox Terrier.name: Smooth Fox Terrier
Smooth Fox Terrier.summary: A lively, smooth-coated English terrier bred to chase foxes out of their dens during hunts.
funFacts: The AKC showed Smooth and Wire Fox Terriers as one breed until 1985.
Nipper, the dog in the "His Master's Voice" logo, is often said to have been part Smooth Fox Terrier.

Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier.name: Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier
Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier.summary: A cheerful Irish farm terrier with a silky, wheat-colored coat and a famously enthusiastic greeting.
funFacts: Wheatens greet people by bouncing up joyfully — fans call it the "Wheaten greetin'."
Puppies are born dark; the coat lightens to wheaten by about age two.

Staffordshire Bull Terrier.name: Staffordshire Bull Terrier
Staffordshire Bull Terrier.summary: A muscular, affectionate English terrier from Staffordshire, one of the UK's most popular family dogs.
funFacts: In the UK it's nicknamed the "nanny dog" for its fondness for children.
It's one of the most popular breeds in the United Kingdom.

Standard Schnauzer.name: Standard Schnauzer
Standard Schnauzer.summary: The original schnauzer, a bearded German farm dog that guarded property and caught vermin.
funFacts: The Miniature and Giant Schnauzers were both developed from it.
Standard Schnauzers appear in paintings by Albrecht Dürer from around 1500.

Sussex Spaniel.name: Sussex Spaniel
Sussex Spaniel.summary: A low, golden-liver spaniel from Sussex, bred to flush game in dense undergrowth while barking.
funFacts: Unlike most spaniels, it barks while hunting, which hunters call "giving tongue."
A Sussex named Stump won Westminster in 2009 at age 10, the oldest winner ever.

Tibetan Mastiff.name: Tibetan Mastiff
Tibetan Mastiff.summary: An ancient Himalayan guardian with a lion-like mane, bred to protect monasteries and nomads' flocks.
funFacts: A Tibetan Mastiff puppy was reportedly sold in China for about $1.5 million in 2011.
Its thick double coat lets it shrug off Himalayan winters.

Tibetan Terrier.name: Tibetan Terrier
Tibetan Terrier.summary: A shaggy Tibetan companion dog — not actually a terrier — kept by monks as a good-luck charm.
funFacts: Its large, flat "snowshoe" feet help it travel over snow.
Tibetans considered them bringers of luck and gave them as gifts rather than selling them.

Toy Terrier.name: Toy Terrier
Toy Terrier.summary: A small, sleek black-and-tan terrier, essentially a toy-sized Manchester Terrier, bred as a ratter and companion.
Toy Terrier.group: Toy variety of the Manchester Terrier
funFacts: In the U.S., it's shown as the Toy variety of the Manchester Terrier.
Its upright, candle-flame-shaped ears are a breed signature.

Treeing Walker Coonhound.name: Treeing Walker Coonhound
Treeing Walker Coonhound.summary: A fast, tricolor American coonhound descended from English Foxhounds, bred to chase raccoons up trees.
funFacts: It descends in part from a stolen dog named Tennessee Lead, bred into Walker foxhounds in the 1800s.
Coonhound fans call it "the people's choice."

Vizsla.name: Vizsla
Vizsla.summary: A sleek, golden-rust Hungarian pointer bred for falconry and bird hunting, famous for its affectionate nature.
funFacts: Vizslas are nicknamed "Velcro dogs" because they stick so close to their owners.
A Vizsla named Chartay was the first dog to earn AKC championships in five different sports.

Weimaraner.name: Weimaraner
Weimaraner.summary: A sleek, silver-gray German hunting dog bred by nobles of the Weimar court to hunt big game.
funFacts: Its silvery coat and light eyes earned it the nickname "Gray Ghost."
Photographer William Wegman's Weimaraners have appeared on Sesame Street.

Welsh Springer Spaniel.name: Welsh Springer Spaniel
Welsh Springer Spaniel.summary: A red-and-white Welsh gundog, a little smaller than the English Springer, bred to flush birds in rough country.
funFacts: It only comes in one color combination: red and white.
Welshies are known for the stamina to hunt all day in rugged terrain.

West Highland White Terrier.name: West Highland White Terrier
West Highland White Terrier.summary: A plucky white Scottish terrier bred to hunt rats, foxes and badgers among the Highland rocks.
funFacts: Legend says Colonel Edward Malcolm started breeding white terriers after mistaking his reddish terrier for a fox.
A Westie is the face of Cesar dog food.

Whippet.name: Whippet
Whippet.summary: A lightning-fast English sighthound bred by miners for racing and rabbit coursing, calm and cuddly at home.
funFacts: Whippets can reach about 35 mph and are known for incredible acceleration.
They were nicknamed "the poor man's racehorse."

Wire Fox Terrier.name: Wire Fox Terrier
Wire Fox Terrier.summary: A jaunty, wire-coated English fox terrier and the most successful breed in Westminster Best in Show history.
funFacts: Wire Fox Terriers have won Best in Show at Westminster 15 times, more than any other breed.
Snowy, Tintin's faithful companion, is a Wire Fox Terrier.
Asta in The Thin Man films was a Wire Fox Terrier.

Wirehaired Pointing Griffon.name: Wirehaired Pointing Griffon
Wirehaired Pointing Griffon.summary: A shaggy, bearded all-purpose gundog developed in the late 1800s by Dutch breeder Eduard Korthals.
funFacts: In Europe it's known as the Korthals Griffon.
Its harsh coat protects it in thick brush and cold water.

Xoloitzcuintli.name: Xoloitzcuintli
Xoloitzcuintli.summary: An ancient Mexican breed, mostly hairless, revered by the Aztecs and named after the god Xolotl.
funFacts: The Aztecs believed Xolos guided souls through the underworld.
Dante in Pixar's Coco is a Xoloitzcuintli.
It's the national dog of Mexico.

Yorkshire Terrier.name: Yorkshire Terrier
Yorkshire Terrier.summary: A tiny, glamorous terrier with a silky blue-and-tan coat, originally bred to catch rats in Yorkshire mills.
funFacts: A Yorkie named Smoky served in World War II and is considered one of the first therapy dogs.
A Yorkie's coat is closer in texture to human hair than to typical dog fur.
